messages:
Priya: FYI support escalated — ACME seeing p99 spikes on /v1/generate (08:10-08:35 UTC). They hit their SLO and reported timeouts.
Maya: On it. Any traces or request ids?
Priya: CS pasted a few request_ids: r_8a7f3, r_b21c9. They say it started after a traffic increase at 08:05.
Alex: Quick glance at cache metrics — prefix_kv_miss_rate jumped from ~8% -> ~42% at 08:08 for shard eu-west-1-pool-5.
Sam: Grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/d/kv/kv-metrics?from=1678836600000&to=1678838400000 — p95/p99 line up with the miss rate jump.
Alex: Also seeing CPU waiting on io for `prefix_lookup` path, and tail latency for the inference worker increases when miss_rate high.
Jin: Can you paste a small log snippet?
Priya: Log snippet from their request (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-15T08:11:04Z] ERROR prefix_cache: miss key='prefix:api:v1:session:abcd1234' latency=118ms
[2026-03-15T08:11:04Z] INFO shard=eu-west-1-pool-5 request_id=r_8a7f3 route=/v1/generate model=redwood-large
[2026-03-15T08:11:05Z] WARN kv_warmup: eviction_triggered lru_size=12000 ttl_seconds=0
```
Maya: That `ttl_seconds=0` stands out — eviction policy seems to be immediate for some keys. Did someone flip TTLs?
Alex: No config flip on control plane in the past 24h per deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: No rollout for prefix_warmup or kv-config in last 48 hours.
Sam: I dug into key distributions — high-cardinality header `x-session-id` is being used raw in prefix key. Miss rate correlates with session id entropy burst from a downstream SDK version.
Priya: Customer mentioned they upgraded their client to `acme-sdk@2.7.0` around 08:04. Could be generating unique session IDs per request.
Jin: Repro steps (local):
1) run loop (100 req/s) with random session header
2) query `/v1/generate` with `x-session-id` varying
Expected: KV warmup should absorb prefixes; Observed: miss_rate climbs and latency increases.
Command: `for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "x-session-id: $RANDOM-$RANDOM" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate; done`
Maya: Sounds like two things: (A) spike in key cardinality (client bug) and (B) eviction policy or warmup drip not handling the surge.
Alex: Temporary mitigations we can apply server-side: increase prefix cache capacity for eu-west-1-pool-5, enable staged warmup (drip) and set a moderate TTL (e.g., 30s) for newly minted prefix entries.
Jin: I'll prepare a flagged rollout: `prefix_cache.pool.eu-west-1-pool-5.capacity += 50%` and `prefix_warmup.stagger_ms=25` for just ACME's tenant id.
Maya: Also let's normalize keys at ingress: strip long session fragments past 32 chars and hash them — that avoids explosion while we patch SDK.
Sam: I can push a transient admission filter that canonicalizes `x-session-id` to `sha1(x-session-id)[0:8]` for tenants opted into esc mitigation.
Priya: CS asked for ETA. Jin?
Jin: I'll roll the per-tenant config change now under a feature flag, monitor for 10m, then widen if stable. Target +5m for rollout, +30m for observation.
ops-bot: Noted incident ticket #INC-2026-0331 created and linked to the thread.
Maya: Also add a metric alarm: if prefix_kv_miss_rate > 20% for > 5m, auto-apply warmup drip.
Alex: We should also audit key normalization logic — I found a bug where empty `x-session-id` values were concatenated with `:` leading to unique suffixes (racey trim). That explains some of the novel keys.
Priya: Good catch. Can we fix normalization in the next patch (2.3.4)? Jin to own.
Jin: I'll open PR for normalization fix and include unit tests for header trimming and max-length enforcement. Link to draft PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/5123
Priya: Action items summary: Jin - rollout per-tenant cache/tweak + PR for normalization. Sam - deploy admission canonicalizer. Alex - monitor p95/p99 and confirm eviction TTL change. Maya - add auto-alarm. Priya - keep CS updated and ask ACME to hold non-essential deploys.
Sam: Rolling the admission filter to canary now for tenant ACME :rocket:.
Jin: Feature flag enabled for ACME on eu-west-1-pool-5 — initial metrics look promising, miss_rate down to ~12% after 2min.
Alex: p99 decreased from 1.8s -> 420ms in the canary shard.
Priya: :thumbsup: notify CS and ask ACME to validate.
Priya: Follow-up: schedule post-mortem after stabilization and include SDK vendor; mark root cause as "unbounded session-id cardinality + missing ingress normalization + aggressive eviction config".
Maya: Will add to post-mortem template and include recommended runbook steps.
Priya: Thanks team, closing thread once CS confirms acceptance.
